name: PinMarks
author: PinMarks

sections.description:
PinMarks adds a feedback button to your site. Your team, clients and visitors can report issues with annotated screenshots, and technical details are attached automatically. Reports show up in your PinMarks project and can be sent to the tools you already use.

Set up in a minute: install, click “Connect with PinMarks” (or paste your project key), done.

Built for WordPress

  • Connect popup – pick or create a PinMarks project without copying keys.
  • Smart visibility – show the button to everyone, logged-in users or specific roles; limit it by post type, post status or URL (with wildcards); or show it only on staging sites.
  • Logged-in users identified – no name and email fields for people who are signed in to WordPress.
  • WordPress details with every report – WordPress and PHP version, theme, active plugins, page builder, a direct edit link and WooCommerce cart context (requires custom metadata to be enabled on your PinMarks project).
  • Admin bar menu – report an issue or switch the widget on and off from the toolbar.
  • Shortcode and block – [pinmarks_button label="Report an issue"] or the “PinMarks report button” block.

A free or paid PinMarks account is required. Sign up at pinmarks.in.

External services

This plugin connects to the PinMarks service (app.pinmarks.in), operated by ScaleStation, to provide the feedback widget.

What it is and what it is used for: on the pages where the widget is shown, the plugin loads the widget script from https://app.pinmarks.in/widget.js. The widget lets people submit feedback, and sends it to your PinMarks project.

What data is sent and when:

  • When a page that shows the widget loads, the visitor’s browser requests the widget script and the widget settings for your project key from app.pinmarks.in. This includes the visitor’s IP address and browser details, as with any web request.
  • Only when a person chooses to submit feedback: their message, an annotated screenshot, the page address, browser and device details, console and network error logs (if enabled in your PinMarks project), and any name and email they enter.
  • If “Identify logged-in users automatically” is enabled (default), the WordPress display name and email of the logged-in user are passed to the widget and sent along with their feedback.
  • If “Send WordPress environment details with reports” is enabled (default), WordPress and PHP version, theme, active plugins, page details and, for WooCommerce sites, cart contents are attached to submitted feedback.
  • When you use “Connect with PinMarks” in the settings page, your browser opens a popup on app.pinmarks.in where you sign in and choose a project; the project key is passed back to your settings page. Your site address is sent so the key is only delivered to your site.

Nothing is sent to PinMarks until a project key is saved and the widget is enabled.

This service is provided by ScaleStation: Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin and activate it.
  2. Go to Settings > PinMarks and click “Connect with PinMarks”, or paste your project key.
  3. Visit your site; the feedback button appears.
sections.faq:
Where do I find my project key?

In your PinMarks project settings. Or just use “Connect with PinMarks” and it is filled in for you.

The button does not show on my site.

Check that the plugin is connected and enabled, and that your visibility settings (users, post types, URL rules, staging only) allow the current page. If you use a caching or optimization plugin, exclude app.pinmarks.in/widget.js from minification, combining and delay.

Can I show the button only after cookie consent?

Yes. Return false from the pinmarks_should_load filter until consent is given.

Are WordPress details stored in my PinMarks project?

They are stored when custom metadata is enabled for your PinMarks project (Agency plan).
